issues.description: Key acceptance policy is complected with widget hide/forward logic inside keyPressEvent
issues.detail: The new branch braids three concerns: reading config, deciding whether a key accepts the completion, and re-dispatching the event to the textedit. The decision 'is this key an accept key?' is a pure function of (key, config) and should be named as one. Right now the policy lives mid-method, mixed with the place-oriented widget state machine, so no one can test or reuse it without instantiating the whole popup.

issues.description: Config name says 'use Enter' but the implementation actually means 'only Tab accepts'
issues.detail: The flag is read inside a branch that already matched Enter/Return/Tab, and the guard fires for any key in that set that is not Tab. The value 'use_enter_for_completions' is therefore not a fact about Enter; it is a fact about which keys are accept keys. The name and the semantics have drifted, which is exactly the kind of incidental confusion that bites later when a third accept key is proposed.

issues.description: Accept-key set is implicit data scattered across the method instead of one named value
issues.detail: The outer branch enumerates Return/Enter/Tab; the new code re-checks Tab by negation. The set of accept keys is a small piece of data that wants to be named once (a tuple, or a config-derived sequence) and consulted, not rediscovered by inverse logic. Naming it would make the Enter-disable option a one-line filter over that set.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keystroke instead of treating the policy as a value
issues.detail: Each keypress re-reads the config through the plugin lookup. That is easy (familiar pattern) but not simple: it complects 'what is the current accept policy' with 'how do I ask the config system right now'. Caching the policy on the widget and updating it on config-change signals would separate read-time from decide-time and make the popup independently testable.

issues.description: Forwarding the event by calling textedit.keyPressEvent re-enters the widget tree by hand
issues.detail: Hiding the popup and then manually invoking the parent's keyPressEvent encodes an assumption about Qt's event routing that the rest of the file does not state. If Enter should fall through to the editor when the popup is dismissed, that is a time-and-identity question (which widget owns this event at which moment) worth saying out loud in a comment or, better, by letting the event propagate naturally via ignore().

review.summary: The feature is small and the default preserves prior behavior, which is the right call. But the implementation is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: a policy question ('which keys accept a completion?') has been wedged into the middle of a keyPressEvent as an inverted Tab check, with a config name that no longer matches what the code actually decides. The accept-key set wants to be named data, the policy wants to be a pure function of (key, config), and the widget should consult that function rather than re-deriving it per keystroke. The question that should have been asked first: what is the set of accept keys, and where does it live?
